key_insight: LLMs can answer medical questions correctly in clean settings yet still lose the right answer when exposed to misleading clinical context, revealing weak epistemic resilience.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare-facing AI, high exam scores are not enough; systems also need to stay reliable when users or prompts contain false or persuasive medical details.
method: Built MedMisBench with 10,932 medical question items and 48,889 misleading context-option pairs.
Tested 11 model configurations across medical reasoning, agentic capability, and patient-journey scenarios.
Measured how often correct answers flipped under targeted misleading context, including authority-framed and exception-based attacks.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated models, accuracy dropped from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked prompt attacks, so real-world clinical risk will also depend on user behavior, deployment safeguards, and local validation.
paper_title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
